eventFixtureFinalReview.scope: Independent read-only review of MenuPadScopeTests scroll fixture EventSystem cleanup, Stage6
confirmedFacts: UGUI EventSystem.OnEnable appends to the static registry; OnDisable removes one reference.
The scroll fixture manually invokes OnEnable for its own EventSystem but previously only destroyed that object.
Observed registry contains two CLR-non-null / Unity-null wrappers while sceneEvents is empty. This explains strict NUnit null assertion failure.
The late scroll fixture can contaminate a following no-domain-reload run; its position after the failing early Content case is consistent with this cross-run path.
limits: The registry receipt alone does not map the two destroyed instance IDs to a captured ScrollEventSystem allocation.
No Unity operations or tests were executed by this reviewer.
Product UIRuntimeManager and strict current-null assertion are unchanged.

findings.description: If the new AreNotSame assertion throws, the following DestroyImmediate(root) is skipped. The List/ScrollRect/Button fixture must be destroyed in an outer finally even when unregister/assert fails.
findings.status: resolved: nested finally always destroys self-owned EventSystem and outer finally always destroys UI root, including unregister assertion failure

eventFixtureFinalReview.recommendedFix: Keep the unregister assertion and ensure both self-owned EventSystem and UI root destruction execute via nested finally.
eventFixtureFinalReview.reReview: Read final nested cleanup source. Strict null/current assertion and original navigation assertions are unchanged. No product modifications or global registry reset introduced.
